Risk Title: Terminated users retain active ERP access
Description: Control 1 test: U1003 (terminated 2026-05-15) and U1010 (terminated 2026-06-02) were still Active in the finance ERP at the 2026-06-15 audit date.
Mitigation / Response: Disable both accounts now; trigger deprovisioning from HR termination events; reconcile HR terminations to active accounts monthly.

Description: Control 2 test: U1010 (last review 2025-11-01) and U1016 (2025-09-01) are past the six-month review cycle.
Mitigation / Response: Complete the overdue reviews; calendar semi-annual recertification with manager sign-off tracked to completion.

Description: Control 3 test: CH-2203 and CH-2207 had no approver; CH-2206 was approved (2026-05-18) after it was implemented (2026-05-14); CH-2208 was self-approved.
Mitigation / Response: Block deployment in the ticketing system until an independent approval is logged; prevent requester from approving own change; review the four changes after the fact.

Risk Title: AP and Purchasing roles held by one user
Description: Control 4 test: U1016 holds AP Clerk and Purchasing Agent, so one person can create a purchase order and process its payment.
Mitigation / Response: Remove the Purchasing Agent role, or add supervisor review of all payments this user processes until it is removed.

Risk Title: Customer database reachable from the public internet
Description: The customer database server has accepted connections from any public address since launch. Assessment scored data exfiltration 3x3 on a 1-3 scale; rescored 4x5 here.
Mitigation / Response: Restrict inbound access to an allow-list of office and VPN egress addresses; require MFA for administrative access.

Risk Title: Automated scanners find the exposed database
Description: Public database ports are scanned continuously and can become a foothold for further attacks. Assessment scored 3x2; rescored 5x3 here.
Mitigation / Response: Same allow-list as R-05; alert on connection attempts from outside the allow-list.

Risk Title: Employee alters or deletes customer records
Description: A malicious or careless employee changes or deletes records, disrupting sales operations. Assessment scored 2x2; rescored 2x3 here.
Mitigation / Response: Role-based access with read-only query access for sales staff; audit logging on write operations.

Description: The assessment recommended moving from SSL to TLS 1.2 or higher on all permitted connections because SSL has known weaknesses.
Mitigation / Response: Disable SSL, enforce TLS 1.2 or higher, and confirm with a configuration scan.

Description: Critical CVE identified on the production ERP application server; no patch applied yet.
Mitigation / Response: Apply the vendor patch in the next maintenance window; add a compensating WAF rule in the interim.

Risk Title: No MFA on remote VPN access
Description: Remote access to the internal network does not require multi-factor authentication.
Mitigation / Response: Roll out MFA enforcement for all VPN users.

Description: The organization has no documented, tested runbook for a ransomware scenario.
Mitigation / Response: Draft the runbook and run a tabletop exercise to test it.

Risk Title: Shared admin credentials on legacy file server
Description: A legacy file server uses one shared administrator account instead of individual accounts.
Mitigation / Response: Migrate to individual admin accounts with logging enabled.

Risk Title: Backup restoration untested for over a year
Description: The restoration procedure for the financial database had not been tested in over a year.
Mitigation / Response: Run and document a full restoration test.

Description: Payroll data was found in unencrypted spreadsheets on a shared drive.
Mitigation / Response: Move the data to an access-controlled system and encrypt existing files.

Risk Title: Critical vendor risk assessments out of date
Description: Several critical vendors have not been reassessed in over 18 months.
Mitigation / Response: Reassess all critical vendors now and move to a 12-month cycle.
